title: Prime-degree towers over algebraically closed residue and divisible values
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value [def-weil-field]. Set $K^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde K=K^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_K=|K^\times|$. Assume $\widetilde K$ is algebraically closed and $\Gamma_K$ is divisible: for each integer $n>0$ every element of $\Gamma_K$ has an $n$th root in $\Gamma_K$. Let $L/K$ be a finite field extension with a compatible nonarchimedean absolute value. Then $\widetilde L=\widetilde K$ and $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_K$. If $\operatorname{char}\widetilde K=0$, then $L=K$. If $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde K>0$, there is a finite tower $K=K_0\subset K_1\subset\cdots\subset K_n=L$, with $n\ge0$ and $[K_{i+1}:K_i]=p$ for every $i<n$. Here finite means finite vector-space dimension.

source.place: §2.1, discussion of maximal moderately ramified extensions preceding Lemma 2.1.5, printed p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.3.1, type 4 paragraph, printed p. 50.

proof.text: For any finite valued extension $M/K$, [lem-trf-valued-extension-degree-bound] gives finite $f=[\widetilde M:\widetilde K]$ and $e=[\Gamma_M:\Gamma_K]$. Every $a\in\widetilde M$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\widetilde K$, since $1,a,\ldots,a^f$ are linearly dependent. That polynomial splits into linear factors over the algebraically closed field $\widetilde K$; their product vanishes at $a$, so one factor does, and $a$ belongs to the image of $\widetilde K$. For $\gamma\in\Gamma_M$, two among $1,\gamma,\ldots,\gamma^e$ have the same coset, so $\gamma^r\in\Gamma_K$ for some $r>0$. Divisibility gives $\delta\in\Gamma_K$ with $\delta^r=\gamma^r$. Positive real numbers have unique positive $r$th roots, hence $\gamma=\delta$. Thus $e=f=1$ for every such $M$, in particular for $L$. Residue-field equality means equality after the canonical embedding.

source.place: Temkin, §2.1, fundamental inequality, printed pp. 7–8; Lemma 2.1.5 and preceding ramification discussion, p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.3.1, pp. 49–50. Primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus], the defect $d(M/K)=[M:K]/(ef)$ is $1$ in residue characteristic zero, and a power of the positive residue characteristic $p$ otherwise. The preceding step gives $[M:K]=d(M/K)$. In characteristic zero apply this with $M=L$: a one-dimensional field extension is the base field, since its nonzero vector $1$ is a basis. In positive residue characteristic this gives $[L:K]=p^a$ for some $a\ge0$.

source.place: Temkin, §2.1, fundamental inequality, printed pp. 7–8; Lemma 2.1.5 and preceding ramification discussion, p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.3.1, pp. 49–50. Primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Any finite tame extension $K^\prime/K$ is trivial. Indeed step 1, which was proved for arbitrary finite $M/K$, gives $e(K^\prime/K)=f(K^\prime/K)=1$. Tameness includes $d(K^\prime/K)=1$ by the definition in [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus]. The defining equation $[K^\prime:K]=efd$ therefore gives degree one and $K^\prime=K$.

source.place: Temkin, §2.1, fundamental inequality, printed pp. 7–8; Lemma 2.1.5 and preceding ramification discussion, p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.3.1, pp. 49–50. Primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Now suppose $p>0$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-trf-valued-tame-prime-tower] with $A=K$ and $B=L$: completeness and the compatible nontrivial real absolute values are precisely our hypotheses, and step 2 supplies the required $p$-power degree. It gives a finite tame extension $K^\prime/K$ in a common algebraic closure and a finite tower from $K^\prime$ to $LK^\prime$, all nonidentity successive degrees being $p$. Step 3 gives $K^\prime=K$, hence $LK^\prime=L$. Delete repeated adjacent fields to obtain the asserted strictly increasing tower. When $L=K$, take the tower of length zero. No separability of $L/K$ was assumed by the cited clause.

Step 3 is genuinely elementary: tame means d=1, so efd=1 and K'=K. Step 4 uses tame-prime-tower (1) with A=K, B=L. Completeness, p>0 and p-power degree (step 2) hold, A'=K by step 3, so LA'=L.
